messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] prefix-cache-health degrade in us-west-2 (p95 latency > 2s, error spike). auto-paging to #incidents. page: @rachelle_oncall

jordan: seeing a subset of tenants getting 502s from prefix read path, started ~00:07 UTC. p95 token latency jumped. not global but correlated to requests hitting cache-lookup v2.

li: logs show repeated KV checksum mismatches for prefixes starting with 'user:' -> fallback to DB read path. sample: `ERR prefix_kv:checksum_mismatch key=user:acct123`

marco: repro locally with a small synthetic load, looks like a cache shard became degraded and returning partial parse results, runtime then triggers a correctness bypass which causes DB read storms.

jordan: customer impact: about 8 tenants, intermittent 502/504, increased cost due to DB amplification. frontline SLOs hit for those tenants.

rachelle_oncall: I'm on it. quick mitigation plan: 1) isolate bad cache shard with route-surgeon, 2) apply temporary tenant quotas to noisy tenants, 3) enable global read-bypass for affected prefixes but only for consistency-critical tenants, 4) disable prefetch for prefix caching to reduce background load. will coordinate comms.

marco: running route-surgeon now to remove shard s-17 from prefix-read ring. command: ```
# remove shard s-17 from prefix reads
redwoodctl routing remove-shard --env production --shard s-17 --service prefix-read
```

incident-bot: route-surgeon job queued: job_id=rs-20260314-7, started by marco. ETA ~30s.

li: applying temporary tenant quotas to top noisy tenants. script: ```
for TENANT in tenant-alpha tenant-gamma tenant-delta; do
  redwoodctl quota set --tenant $TENANT --rate 80r/s --burst 200
done
```

marco: applied; verified 200->80r/s cap on listed tenants. traffic to DB from those tenants down 65% in 2 mins.

rachelle_oncall: enabling prefix-level read-bypass for these tenants for correctness (this forces reads to authoritative DB rather than attempting cache read/validate). only for prefixes matching `user:` and `session:`. command: ```
redwoodctl cache policy set --scope tenant --pattern "^user:|^session:" --policy bypass --tenants tenant-alpha,tenant-gamma,tenant-delta
```

sre-runbook-bot: WARNING: bypass policy increases per-token cost and latencies; monitor DB CPU and p95. Runbooks: cache-bypass -> monitor-db-heatmap, reduce-prefetch.

jordan: disabling prefetch for prefix-cache globally for a short window: ```
redwoodctl cache config update --module prefix-prefetch --enabled false --reason "emergency: reduce background churn"
```

incident-bot: action applied: prefix-prefetch disabled.

product-ops: heads-up — three customers (acct-987, acct-345, acct-120) may see degraded latency. drafting proactive comms.

li: telemetry: p95 tokens for affected tenants back down to ~1.1s from 2.6s; error rate reduced by 78%. DB write/reads still elevated but within emergency quotas so far.

marco: shard s-17 confirmed unhealthy, removed from ring. need to rebuild it offline and run integrity sweep before returning. proposing: mark s-17 quarantined and schedule maintenance window.

rachelle_oncall: handing off to next on-call @marco in 30m for follow-up and rebuild. current mitigations remain: shard quarantined, tenant quotas, prefix bypass for affected tenants, prefetch disabled.

marco: acknowledged. I'll own the rebuild and integrity check. next actions: 1) run kv-sweep job on s-17, 2) reconcile prefix checksums across replicas, 3) communicate to CS with ETA.

jordan: quick customer impact summary for CS: "Limited subset of tenants experienced elevated errors and latency due to a degraded cache shard triggering correctness fallbacks. We isolated the shard, applied temporary rate limits and targeted cache bypass for affected prefixes, and disabled prefetch to reduce load. Most customers recovered with normal latency; we are rebuilding the shard and will follow up with a full postmortem and RCA."

product-ops: thanks — sending comms now. cc @marco for technical follow-ups.

sre-runbook-bot: Recommended post-incident tasks (auto-generated): [1] run full KV integrity sweep on quarantined shard (cmd: `redwoodctl shard sweep --shard s-17 --level full`), [2] validate prefix checksums across 3 replicas, [3] re-enable prefetch after observing DB load < 60% for 15m, [4] prepare customer-facing RCA draft.

rachelle_oncall: handing incident to marco. I'm available if anything spikes. logging timeline and adding to pager duty notes. :white_check_mark:

marco: starting sweep now, will post progress here.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations active: shard-quarantine, tenant-rate-caps, prefix-read-bypass (targeted), prefetch-disabled. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring.

jordan: thanks team. once rebuild complete let's coordinate a canary reintroduce of shard and roll prefetch carefully.

marco: update 00:34 UTC — sweep running, 0/3 checksum mismatches found after repair attempt, continuing replication catch-up. expected completion ~00:55 UTC.

rachelle_oncall: closing immediate paging loop. if anything new pops, re-open thread or page next oncall.

product-ops: filed customer notes and scheduled proactive emails to affected tenants.

marco: post-incident checklist I'll handle: create postmortem draft, run deeper artifact collection, propose longer-term fixes (health probes on prefix shards, better prefetch backoff heuristics, tenant auto-backpressure).

jordan: adding an eval test to catch similar checksum regressions in the next release candidate.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigations active -> stabilized. next_update ETA 02:00 UTC for postmortem draft.
